summary: Comprehensive backend + frontend testing of GigBlast platform. 35/35 backend pytest tests passed (auth, gigs CRUD, accept/withdraw, blast in_app/email/sms graceful, notifications, profile uploads, file ACL, admin endpoints). UI flow validated: admin login, dialog-based gig creation, worker register, feed visibility, gig acceptance, logout for both roles. All endpoints listed in the review request are working.

minor.issue: Email stored lowercased but request payload preserves case — tests must compare case-insensitively. Documented in tests; not user-facing.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py is ~900+ lines — fine for MVP but recommend splitting routers (auth, gigs, profile, admin) into modules once feature surface grows.
Email normalization: backend lowercases emails on register/login (good). Consider returning normalized email consistently from /auth/me.
Blast endpoint correctly wraps email/sms providers in try/except and increments blast_count even when external creds missing — graceful degradation verified.
File ACL on /api/files/{path} correctly enforces owner-or-admin (verified 403 for other workers).
Slots filling flips status to 'filled' automatically — verified.
test_credentials: Admin: admin@gigblast.com / GigBlast2026! (read from /app/memory/test_credentials.md). Workers created dynamically with TEST_ / ui_ prefix.
seed_data_creation: Test gigs were created and deleted during pytest run (cleaned up via DELETE). One residual gig may be left from the UI test flow (acceptances test only, low volume).
context_for_next_testing_agent: backend_test.py is a complete regression suite, 35 tests, ~5s runtime. Email comparisons must be case-insensitive (backend lowercases). worker_logout uses data-testid='worker-logout-btn', admin uses 'admin-logout-btn'. CreateGigDialog has full data-testid coverage. Worker feed empty-state message: 'No open gigs right now. Check back soon.'
rca of the issue: No bugs found. Initial test failures during authoring were test-script issues (case sensitivity + fixture/test ordering), all resolved.
